- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peaks by 15–30% for spikes.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33), model underestimates; increase low-range forecasts by 10–25% to avoid under-shock.
- Model consistently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive; apply downward bias to first 5–7 days.
- After a sharp spike in true outcome, model often overshoots in the following 3–5 days; apply smoothing decay (e.g., 0.85 multiplier) to subsequent forecasts.
- Mean reversion is strong in 10–15 day horizon; if forecast deviates >1.5σ from recent 7-day average, adjust toward historical mean.
- Sentiment volatility >0.3 in 3 consecutive days triggers model overconfidence; reduce forecast variance by 20–40% for volatile sentiment periods.
